system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

diacritics.note: Dot vs colon after a digit changes its letter; dots/colons/bars around a Latin letter select the code word.

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE login cookie (earlier session); set the target.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R9248-R9254 images and key record R9262 with the saved cookie.
R9262 is Throckmorton's cipher, not Smith's; the API listing of neighbouring key records found R9261, 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (f. 179).
Applied the key to 17 Jan 1562/3 passages: 'chief ... side' read at once.
CSP Foreign vol. 6 no. 109 cites Forbes ii 287; Forbes vol. 2 OCR on archive.org prints the letter; the reading matches. Add MS 4136 identified as Forbes's deciphering file.
Transcribed and read the 1564 Arles 24 Nov passage from the glyphs; matches the CSP no. 815 summary.
First parallel agent on the 1564-65 letters read only parts of two letters.
Agents read R9249 and R9250 letters (27 Jan and 13 Apr 1563 in full, 1563/4-1566 in part) and the 1564-65 letters in R9252-R9254 (most in large part), checking against Forbes and CSP.
Readings agree with Forbes's printed text and CSP summaries; two date corrections (Avignon 4 Oct not 27 Oct 1564; 22 Mar 1565/6 not 1566/7).
R9236 (f.140) fetched from DECODE; five letters' cipher passages on one leaf, nulls London/Lyn/Poole/Dover/Hastings/Garnesey identify Smith's key.
Two agents deciphered the passages sign by sign with key R9261; new variant: double bar = i.
15 Oct and 15/17 Dec 1562 agree with Forbes ii 119 and 238; 20 Oct 1562, 4 Nov 1563 and 31 Jan 1562/3 not found in Forbes, read from glyphs only.

Located 20 Oct 1562 in Forbes ii 122 (CSP F. 5 no. 880) and 4 Nov 1563 in CSP F. 6 no. 1366; resolved 'garden'/'side'/'chamillion' and 'La Rochelle'. 31 Jan 1562/3 advertisements not found in print; only (2) 'queen of Navarre' read.

31 Jan 1562/3 advertisements: searched CSP F. 6 (21 Jan-10 Feb 1563) and Forbes ii Jan-Feb 1563; no printed text. Full-resolution re-read gives only '(1) Monsieur de [L]uy', '(2) the queen of Navarre', last line '… band that [K. of Navarre/Fr. King] and …'; CSP has 'the Queen of Navarre's band' in Warwick's news of late Jan 1563 as context only.

outcome.method_basis: The key is filed in the same manuscript as the letters: DECODE R9261 p. 1 = Add MS 4136 f. 179, 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher', in Forbes's deciphering file; the readings were checked against Forbes's A Full View (1740-41) and CSP Foreign.
outcome.notes: Most passages read; code signs in the hooked-T family read from context. 12 Mar 1562/3 not transcribed (in Forbes). The 1563/4-1566 verbatim passages were only summarised in print before. R9236 (f.140, five further letters) added 21 Sept: two agree with Forbes, 4 Nov 1563 read in large part, 20 Oct 1562 and 31 Jan 1562/3 in part.
